summary: Stealth snapshotter IO leak causing gradual GPU bank starvation and autoscaler misclassification
description:
Issue summary: Customer (NimbusDocs, dedicated) reported a steady degradation in p50/p95 throughput over ~6 hours during a midday window. Requests began queuing and GPU attach attempts experienced longer NVLink handshake times. Impact: customer saw 20-40% drop in sustained throughput for batched routes and intermittent 5xx/attach-timeout errors. No direct error spikes in user-facing API logs; degradation was gradual and noisy.

Observed pattern: the cluster showed one or two GPU banks with growing IO stalls correlated with background snapshotter activity on a subset of hosts. Autoscaler telemetry appeared to interpret the stalled attach/heartbeat behavior as healthy (no capacity shortage) and did not trigger scale-up, leading to sustained starvation rather than a short blip.

Why unique: this was not a classic noisy-tenant compute spike — CPU and per-request latency were normal initially. The root cause was low-bandwidth, persistent NVMe read congestion from snapshotting agents that leaked qpair resources and increased PCIe wait, causing GPU bank attach backoff. Because the autoscaler relies on attach success/queue depth signals, it misclassified the state as stable and held capacity steady.

Customer-visible impact: throughput drop on dedicated pool -> higher queue times, some 5xx attach timeouts; billing unaffected.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy a dedicated pool with customers running long-lived batched inference (short streams).
Schedule a background snapshot/backup job on a subset of hosts overlapping peak serving windows that streams checkpoint files to NVMe in small bursts.
Observe slow steady growth in NVMe read latency and qpair exhaustion on affected nodes.
Watch GPU attach handshake time increase and autoscaler telemetry remain within non-failure thresholds, preventing scale-up.

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 11:30 — Support triaged. No obvious model regressions; customer traffic steady. Noted NVMe saturation on subset of hosts via iostat and kernel metrics.
2026-03-10 12:05 — SRE ran az-attach-trace; found consistent attach backoff on hosts with snapshotter activity. Linked to snapshotter PRs that changed chunking behavior last week.
2026-03-10 13:10 — Hypothesis: snapshotter small-chunk read pattern monopolizes NVMe qpair slots, raising latency and causing GPU attach to backoff without explicit driver errors.
2026-03-10 14:02 — Reproduced in staging by running snapshotter in a tight loop; observed same attach-time increase and autoscaler no-op due to telemetry thresholds.
comments: Support (Sofia): Notified customer and requested transient telemetry (iostat, nvme-cli, allocator logs). Customer provided logs from 10:45-13:00 window.
SRE (Jordan): Confirmed NVMe qpair stalls on 2/24 hosts in the dedicated pool. Created hotfix patch to limit snapshotter concurrent read streams per host.

Support (Sofia): Communicated workaround to NimbusDocs — stagger snapshot windows and disable aggressive chunking. Customer accepted and applied stagger; reported throughput recovery to baseline within 30 minutes.
Engineering (Amir Das): Opened PR to add a snapshotter backpressure token bucket and to surface qpair contention to autoscaler signals (see related PR).
resolution: Applied immediate mitigation: 1) instructed customer to stagger snapshot jobs and reduce chunk concurrency (workaround); 2) rolled cluster-level snapshotter limiter on affected hosts to cap concurrent nvme reads; 3) merged autoscaler change to include nvme/qpair contention metric as a negative scale-signal and shipped canary the next morning. Result: throughput returned to expected levels and attach timeouts dropped to baseline. Follow-up: permanent snapshotter fix and autoscaler signal enrichment scheduled (see postmortem items).
postmortem_followup: Add NVMe qpair contention telemetry to autoscaler signals and dashboard (owner: infra-team, ETA: 2 weeks).
Harden snapshotter: implement read-concurrency token bucket and adaptive chunk sizing (owner: snapshotter-team, ETA: 1 week).
Run soak test with synthetic small-chunk snapshot workload + mixed short-stream inference to validate steady-state behavior (owner: SRE, ETA: 1 week).
Customer follow-up call scheduled to review mitigation and confirm satisfactory SLAs (owner: CS, ETA: 2026-03-15).
